text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 PrivateLink connectivity failures observed in eastus3b. Multiple customer endpoints reporting DNS resolution failures and intermittent TCP resets. Auto-escalating to on-call. link: https://redwood.incidents/1759004321

sara: onboarding — I'm on it. pulling recent alerts and checking route table state.

miguel: seeing spike in DNS NXDOMAINs from our edge probes in eastus3b starting ~1759004200. Also elevated RSTs on TLS handshake.

eng-network: quick hypothesis — could be a control-plane glitch causing split view between eastus3b resolver cache and global DNS. Any recent DNS infra deploys?

sara: no DNS deploys in the last 6h. Rolling back nothing. Running targeted digs now.

ryan: customer-reported: "connections to privatelink.mycorp.internal fail, intermittent 522s" — they have endpoints in eastus3b only.

ops-bot: probe results:
```
probe: eastus3b-edge-07 -> dig +short privatelink.mycorp.internal @10.10.10.5
-> response: 0.0.0.0
```

sara: that's odd — receiving 0.0.0.0 as answer from in-region recursive. Running traceroute to resolver.

miguel: looking at route tables and VPC peering state for affected accounts. No peering deletes. BGP sessions to cloud provider SRs show intermittent adjacency drops 1759004205-1759004300 then stable.

eng-network: can someone capture a tcpdump from the resolver host? Collect queries to see if we have DNS rewrite or a null answer source.

ryan: on it — `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 53 -w /tmp/dns-eastus3b.pcap`

sara: mitigation plan step 1: failover PrivateLink control-plane to eastus2 region (manual) for affected customers (temporary). Step 2: force TTL flush on our in-region resolvers and restart resolver pool.

support-lead: contacting customers proactively. Notifying affected accounts and recommending they switch to multi-AZ endpoints if possible.

ops-bot: live tcpdump excerpt (narrowed):
```
15:12:03.123 IP resolver1.10.10.10.53 > edgeprobe.10.20.20.14.12345: 2892 q: A? privatelink.mycorp.internal. + [1au] AAAA? OPT(512)
15:12:03.124 IP resolver1.10.10.10.53 > edgeprobe.10.20.20.14.12345: 2892 *SERVFAIL*
15:12:03.125 IP resolver1.10.10.10.53 > edgeprobe.10.20.20.14.12345: 2892 q: A? privatelink.mycorp.internal. + [1au] AAAA? OPT(512)
15:12:03.126 IP resolver1.10.10.10.53 > edgeprobe.10.20.20.14.12345: 2892 RCODE=0 ANSWER: 0.0.0.0
```

miguel: pattern looks like inconsistent authoritative answers — sometimes SERVFAIL, sometimes a NULL/blackhole IP. Could be a mis-applied DNS response policy (RPZ) or an accidental firewall/NAT affecting responses.

eng-network: checking egress NAT gateway logs and DNS policy engine. Found a recent rule applied at 1759004180 by infra-sa that injects RPZ entries for abuse ranges — rule may have been too greedy and matched internal privatelink names. File: `/etc/dns/policy/rpz-blacklist.conf`

sara: rollback that RPZ entry now. `sudo mv /etc/dns/policy/rpz-blacklist.conf /tmp/` then `systemctl restart redwood-resolver` across pool.

ops-bot: RPZ rollback executed on 6/6 resolvers. Restart propagation in progress.

support-lead: customer update drafted and sent: "We observed a misapplied DNS policy affecting PrivateLink hostnames in eastus3b. Our teams have removed the policy and are restarting resolvers. Please let us know if you see continued failures."

ryan: post-rollback probes: `dig +short privatelink.mycorp.internal @10.10.10.5` -> `10.40.50.60` (correct). Latency to endpoint restored for initial customers.

miguel: BGP session flaps earlier may have been correlated (control plane updates triggered policy push). We'll verify sequence in infra audit logs.

eng-network: next steps — 1) run global consistency check for RPZ rules against internal suffix list; 2) add unit tests to policy push pipeline to prevent wildcard matches against `*.privatelink.*` names; 3) add canary rollout for resolver policy changes.

sara: oncall handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Handoff to miguel for monitoring through the next 3 hours. miguel, please confirm you accepted.

miguel: taking over. I'll maintain watch and run scheduled probes every 5m.

ops-bot: scheduled probes: enabled for privatelink suffix check — 5m frequency. Alerts lowered to P2 if baseline restored for 30m.

support-lead: tagging postmortem: owners = eng-network (primary), infra (policy), ops (runbooks). ETA draft: 48h. Customer CS reps queued for follow-up.

eng-network: quick root-cause note: RPZ policy push had an overly-broad matcher `*.*privatelink*` from a manual update. Combined with transient BGP control-plane flaps this created a window where some resolvers returned poisoned answers or blackhole responses.

sara: closing pager for P1. Reopen if we see recurrence. Great job triaging fast. :thumbsup:

miguel: leaving a checklist for the postmortem: 
- timeline of policy push and BGP flaps
- resolver logs + pcaps
- affected customer list + CS comms
- rollback and verification steps
- prevention: linting policy rules, canary deploy, targeted unit tests

support-lead: filing incident ticket INC-2026-0421 and assigning severity war room for the postmortem review.

incident-bot: Incident closed (P1 -> resolved) at 1759006870. Metrics: ~37 minutes to remediation, impacted 4 enterprise customers, transient errors for internal probes and customer connect attempts.

sara: final note — please review the new policy lint rule PR before it lands. I'll add test cases for privatelink suffixes.
